purpose: Keep public-safe evidence from becoming extractive, falsely complete, or misleading about shared work.

risks.risk: A publicly accessible artifact may still contain people, contexts, or uses that were never consented to as portfolio evidence.
controls: Treat public availability as source accessibility, not blanket permission for republication or emphasis.
Prefer paraphrase, aggregate description, and omission when reuse could create new exposure.
Require explicit approval before featuring identifiable private people, sensitive images, or testimony-like recollections.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any proposed publication that newly centers an identifiable collaborator, participant, image, quotation, or sensitive event.

risks.risk: Collective projects and shared accounts can be misread as sole authorship or ownership.
controls: Separate project outcome, collective contribution, and Jamie's evidenced role.
Use authored only for records with attributable authorship; otherwise use the narrower verb supported by evidence.
Maintain collaborator corroboration and role-narrowing paths.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any claim using founded, led, created, authored, produced, managed, or won in a collective context.

risks.risk: Community, legal, financial, enforcement, housing, and mutual-aid records may expose people or turn vulnerability into professional proof.
controls: Publish the operating contribution without publishing participant-level records.
Keep private correspondence, applicant records, donor data, legal-review material, addresses, and attendance records outside the public repository.
Name omission as an ethical boundary when it is material to understanding the work.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any artifact involving enforcement, legal strategy, financial hardship, residence, attendance, community conflict, or mutual aid.

risks.risk: Code commits, posts, and database rows can make digitally legible work appear more important than facilitation, hosting, repair, field coordination, print production, listening, and handoff.
controls: Pair digital evidence with an offline-evidence question in every project review.
Do not use corpus volume as a proxy for contribution value.
Seek collaborator and material-process evidence for work that left fewer machine-readable traces.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any claim strengthened primarily by record count, commit count, social-account volume, or database recoverability.

risks.risk: Archived services, organizations, offices, domains, programs, and relationships may be described as current after their status changes.
controls: Date status claims and use archived, former, historical, or current only when verified.
Separate historical accomplishment from present availability.
Recheck current contact, domain, service, and institutional status before production release.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any present-tense claim or link about a service, organization, office, program, venue, domain, or collaborator role.

risks.risk: AI-assisted archival synthesis can be mistaken for eyewitness testimony, independent corroboration, or a source that witnessed the original work.
controls: Label AI-assisted review as synthesis and cite the underlying evidence class.
Never attribute an AI-generated proof note to a human collaborator.
Keep interpretation distinct from recovered fact and preserve unresolved questions.
risks.reviewTrigger: Any public wording derived substantially from an AI archive review without direct public or collaborator corroboration.

offlineEvidenceCommitments.commitment: Actively seek evidence of hosting, facilitation, invitation, trust-building, and follow-through rather than reducing participation work to event or post counts.
Document material sequencing, on-site coordination, repair, safety, and trade relationships when assessing built-environment work.
Treat handbills, packets, maps, print production, door-to-door circulation, and neighborhood intake as operating infrastructure.
Preserve how listening, belief, interpretation, and translation carried lived experience into civic or organizational decision surfaces.
Record repair, stewardship, transition, and mission-aligned handoff as outcomes, including when a project appropriately leaves Jamie's custody.
